description: SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to interaction histories, allowing relevant recent and distant actions to influence recommendations. It combines item and positional embeddings, attention and feed-forward blocks, and item-embedding scores. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: Attention balances the simplicity of short-range transition models with the ability to use longer histories. This fits datasets with different interaction densities. However, standard SASRec learns item-ID embeddings and does not directly solve cold start for unseen items or users without histories.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain all four category routes. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the effective 200-epoch default. Select changes using only macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer whenever architecture changes. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), adapting probes to the actual model. No benchmark improvement has been measured here.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark training split.
  Form padded histories and shifted next-item targets.
  Embed item IDs and positions.
  Apply causal self-attention and feed-forward blocks.
  Score positive and sampled negative items by embedding dot products.
  Optimize binary cross-entropy at nonpadding positions.
  Select checkpoints using the prescribed validation protocol.
  Save model weights, configuration, and matching predictor code.
Route inference requests to the corresponding category model.

originality.positive: SASRec provides a principled attention-based sequential recommendation method.
originality.negative: Using SASRec as the supplied SASRec baseline adds little methodological novelty; no concrete cold-start extension is specified.

future_potential.positive: Available titles and descriptions could support a future content-based extension for rare items, subject to validation.
future_potential.negative: That extension is outside standard SASRec, and its benefit on this benchmark remains untested.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing SASRec baseline and compatibility contract reduce implementation effort.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require synchronized training, predictor serialization, and diagnostic probes.
